summary: Rock Creek Guard Station crow's nest, Wasco County, Oregon, per the register: 100-foot nest and camp (1925), USFS cabin (1932); now gone. Register coordinates conflict with its county.

facts.design: 100-foot crow's nest and camp (1925); cabin built by the U.S. Forest Service (1932)
facts.status_note: The register says it is now gone; no source we read describes what, if anything, remains at the site.

corrections.proposed: Unresolved; check before publishing. The register's own county and forest, and Rex's Wasco County page location 4S-11E-25, point to Wasco County, not to these coordinates.
corrections.why: The register gives Wasco County and Mount Hood National Forest, but its coordinates (43.33 N, 123.00 W) lie far to the southwest of Wasco County. The two cannot both be right.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register's county and forest, and Rex's Wasco County page (4S-11E-25, Mount Hood National Forest), agree on Wasco County. The register's coordinates do not. The story reports the conflict and does not pick one.

sources.title: Rock Creek Guard Station Lookout Site
Oregon Lookouts - Forest Fire Lookout Association

notes_for_editor: Three pages. The only history is the register's two-line description (1925 nest and camp, 1932 USFS cabin); Oregon Lookouts has no history block for this site. Location conflict: register coordinates do not match its own county and forest; fix the coordinates before publishing. Oregon Lookouts' Douglas County page does not list a Rock Creek site. A Douglas Forest Protective Association post, seen only as a search snippet (login-walled on fetch, not used as evidence), mentions a Rock Creek Guard Station built in 1952 and destroyed by a fire; it appears to be a different building in Douglas County and is not used. The register's 2011 photo (courtesy of Howard Verschoor) has no URL, so no photo is recorded.
